To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we present DIOC, which is a language for programming safe distributed applications that can be updated at runtime.

we propose DIOC, a programming language for distributed applications that are safe by construction, and that we prove that the semantics of DIOC programs are preserved by a compiler that generates code for each site in a lower-level programming language called DPOCC.
we have developed a language for programming dynamic choreographies and that we have proved the correctness of the translation from dynamic choreographies to dynamic process-oriented choreographies.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design, implementation and formalisation of a language for programming and updating distributed applications.
the design and implementation of a programming language for distributed applications with dynamic choreographies.
the development of safe and flexible programming models for distributed applications, and with the design of languages and compilation techniques that support them.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
DIOC is a programming language that allows programmers to write distributed applications that are safe by construction, and that can be updated at runtime.
we present a programming language for choreographies that allows for dynamic updates, and prove the correctness (in terms of safety) of the updates.
DIOC is a language that supports safe runtime updates of distributed applications.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a language for distributed applications with runtime updates that are free from communication problems by construction.
we present a programming model and a formalisation that allow for safe and efficient runtime updates of distributed applications.
DIOC is a language for programming dynamic distributed choreographies, and that DPOC is a language for executing them.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the correctness of distributed applications is preserved by the runtime updates, even if the application is updated at runtime by an untrusted party.
the choreography style can be used to program distributed applications with runtime updates, and to guarantee the preservation of communication safety properties.
it is possible to build distributed applications that are robust to runtime updates, and that are free from communication problems.
